newsitem.title: INDIA: Low-caste woman sworn in as Indian state leader.
newsitem.headline: Low-caste woman sworn in as Indian state leader.

text.p: A woman leader of a party of low-caste Hindus was sworn in on Friday as chief minister of India's most populous state, ending six months of direct federal rule over the province.

Mayawati, 40, was sworn in two days after her Bahujan Samaj Party and its longtime rival, the right-wing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), agreed to form a government in Uttar Pradesh state, home to some 140 million people.
"My first priority is to establish the rule of law that had been completely eroded during the long spell of President's rule in the state," the chief minister told a news conference.

The northern state, which is bisected by the mighty Ganges River, has been under direct rule by New Delhi since inconclusive local elections last September failed to produce a clear majority for any one political group.
Under a new power-sharing experiment, the BJP will allow the Bahujan Samaj Party to head the two-party coalition government for six months, followed by a six-month turn at the helm by the BJP.
"Since ours is a coalition givernment, we'll have to take many decisions jointly," Mayawati said.
